title: India & Canada sign commercial deals, aim for CEPA by end-2026
content:
India and Canada have signed commercial agreements and MoUs in Karnataka while reaffirming plans to conclude CEPA talks by end-2026. 
The fifth round in Ottawa covered goods, services, investment, rules of origin, intellectual property and trade remedies; the next is due in New Delhi in early November. 
Goods trade was $7.95 billion in 2025-26, down 8.23 per cent.

title: Cotton yarn prices hold steady in south India as buyers stay cautious
content:
Cotton yarn prices stayed steady in Mumbai and Tiruppur after earlier gains, with sentiment split between weak Mumbai demand and firmer export-led support in Tiruppur.
Garment units resisted higher fabric prices amid payment constraints, while firm Indian cotton prices and a favourable rupee–dollar rate aided Tiruppur.
Gujarat cotton stayed stable as mills slowed buying before higher arrivals.

title: China factory-gate inflation hits 5%: Can SS27 buyers protect margins?
content:
China’s producer prices rose 5.0 per cent year on year in September, shifting SS27 sourcing assumptions without proving inputs are rising.
India’s textile WPI rose 13.85 per cent against 3.57 per cent for apparel; China’s clothing producer prices fell 1.2 per cent.
Buyers should stress-test cotton, PTA, MEG and polyester costs, compare equivalent constructions and set benchmark-based clauses.

title: Bangladesh must keep policy tight, pursue reforms: IMF
content:
IMF has urged Bangladesh to keep monetary conditions tight as inflation persisted, averaging 8.65 per cent in September, and said tightening alone would not restore stability. 
It forecast FY2026-27 inflation at 10.9 per cent and flagged fiscal, financial and price pressures. 
Bangladesh sought a new IMF-backed programme in May after halting further disbursements under the previous one.

title: India’s textile & apparel exports rise 17.51% in September
content:
India’s textile and apparel exports grew 17.51 per cent year on year to $3.081 billion in September 2026, with textiles up 19.87 per cent and apparel up 13.68 per cent.
April–September exports rose 2.38 per cent to $18.158 billion, but apparel shipments fell 6.19 per cent.
The sector’s export share declined, while raw cotton and cotton waste imports surged 80.92 per cent in September.

title: Bangladesh garment exporters face pressure from steep US freight
content:
Bangladesh’s exporters warned that high US freight costs, rising raw-material prices and expensive financing were weakening competitiveness. 
Shipping a garment container from Chattogram to New York could cost up to $12,900, above European rates. 
Uncertainty surrounding the Middle East conflict disrupted shipment and production planning, while buyers delayed orders and resisted price increases.

title: EU traceability push puts Bangladesh’s SMEs to the test
content:
Bangladesh’s garment SMEs could face a disproportionate burden from EU traceability and DPP rules as they invest in data collection, verification, system integration and training.
Stakeholders seek clearer rules, coordinated data systems, targeted financing and enough preparation time to prevent smaller suppliers bearing excessive compliance costs.
